title: Monarch for iOS inventory entry
description: One file per web component id: inventory/<id>.json. Validated by Scripts/generate.py, which supports the keywords used here: type, enum, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, minItems, minLength, pattern.

id.description: The web component id from platforms/parity.json. Equal to the file name without .json.

name.description: The primary Swift declaration (ios.name in parity.json), or null when Monarch ships nothing.

family.description: The web family from parity.json, or foundations for entries with no web id.

category.description: A: native adoption. B: Monarch style or wrapper. C: custom.

coverage.description: How the web component is covered on iOS, as in parity.json.

wrapsNative.description: The exact SwiftUI API used. Null only for web-only coverage.

status.description: An experimental entry ships its declarations as @_spi(Experimental) public (checked by Scripts/generate.py).

layer.description: The documentation layer (ADR 0017): patterns are experimental domain composites (AI panels, product screens, composites of one domain); everything else is components. A pattern is always experimental. Equal to the layer of the same id on Android (scripts/native/status-check.mjs).

since.description: The Monarch for iOS version that added the entry.

api.description: Signature strings, as written in the source.

appearance.description: How it looks in the light, dark and high-contrast themes. One or two sentences.

platformNotes.description: How it differs from Android and the web, and why.

tests.description: The test suites that cover the entry.

examples.description: Every example is compiled and rendered by the tests.

code.description: The body of a SwiftUI view.

setup.description: Optional declarations the code needs, placed in the same view: state, environment, functions.

previewPresented.description: For the documentation previews only: the @State variables of setup that start presented in the preview host, so a sheet, alert, dialog, popover or flow is open in the image. A name starts true; name=expr starts as expr. The first example of an entry with this field is the one the preview shows.

previewTap.description: For the documentation previews only: true when the example opens its presentation from its own button (state inside a component), so the preview host activates the first button.

previewScreen.description: For the documentation previews only: true when the capture is the whole screen cut to a presentation that previewAction opens (a sheet opened by an action rather than by a Bool).

previewAction.description: For the documentation previews only: statements the preview host runs once after the example appears, for a state that only an action creates (a toast after a delete, a result after a save). Can use the example's own methods and state.

previewMenu.description: For the documentation previews only: true when the example's menu (a Menu or a context menu) cannot be presented by state, so the preview host opens it.

experimental.description: True when the example of a stable entry uses an experimental symbol. It is then compiled with @_spi(Experimental) import MonarchUI. Examples of an experimental entry need not set it.

imports.description: Optional system frameworks to import besides SwiftUI, MonarchUI and MonarchTokens.

fixture.description: Only on the first example: the id of the parity fixture (packages/react/src/**/<id>.fixture.json) whose scenario this example renders, equal to the entry's id. Its code and setup are then written from template and setupTemplate by scripts/native/fixtures.mjs (CROSS-PLATFORM.md section 8).

webExample.description: With fixture: the title of the web primary example (sections.examples.items[0] in <id>.docs.tsx), checked by scripts/native/fixtures.mjs and scripts/native/status-check.mjs.

template.description: With fixture: the Swift of code with {{path}} placeholders for the fixture's data (filters: tone, case, pascal, double, millis, date, raw). code is generated from it; edit the template, then run npm run native:fixtures.

setupTemplate.description: With fixture: setup with {{path}} placeholders, as template.

webEquivalent.description: The React component name, or null.

dependsOn.description: Inventory ids this entry builds on, as in parity.json.

toneMap.description: The web component's state-to-tone tables this entry reproduces, by the web table name (for example STATE_TONE in ai-spend-cap.tsx): { "<TABLE>": { "<state>": "<tone>" } }. Checked against the web source and this platform's source by scripts/native/parity-lint.mjs.

icons.description: The glyphs the web component draws itself and this entry draws by default: { "<slot>": "<web glyph, a key of platforms/icons.json>" }. Checked by scripts/native/parity-lint.mjs.

parityExceptions.description: Written exceptions to the cross-platform parity rule (CROSS-PLATFORM.md section 8): each names the rule, the reason and the platform convention. Shown on the docs page under Platform behaviour. rule fixture-data with paths waives fixture values the example cannot show.
